confidence_notes: I used web searches to set the food and drink anchors. Expatica (Numbeo data, June 2026) and MyLifeElsewhere (July 2026) closely agree: an inexpensive meal is about $20 (some sources give $24.50 with a drink), a cappuccino about $4.95 and a domestic draft pint about $6. Numbeo's mid-range meal for two (three courses, no drinks) is about $89, with a range of $60 to $125. I found no reliable citywide average for cocktails or wine. Expatistan gives about $15 for a downtown club cocktail, but that is based on only a few data points. Visit Orlando happy-hour listings show $9-10 cocktails and $7-9 wine. So the cocktail and wine figures are bounded estimates based on how those prices relate to beer locally. Prices near the theme parks and on International Drive are higher than the city figures above. Accommodation figures are general model estimates for July 2026, not from searches or listings. Orlando has very few registered hostels, so the dorm and private-hostel prices are the least certain. The basic-hotel figure assumes budget motels in the Kissimmee/US-192 and International Drive areas. The 3-star figure assumes branded midscale hotels during the July summer-holiday season.
comparable_city_reasoning: I treated Orlando as a large, tourism-heavy US Sun Belt metro, priced like Tampa, Jacksonville or Phoenix for restaurants and drinks. Theme-park demand pushes up drink prices in tourist areas. Accommodation is cheaper than in major US gateway cities like New York, Miami or Los Angeles because Orlando has a very large hotel supply.
